data.title: FAA Administrator Bedford warns comms system will "continue to break" without fix
data.description:
A decades-old, antiquated telecommunications system that federal air traffic controllers rely on will continue to have problems until it is properly funded and fully upgraded with modern equipment, according to FAA Administration Bryan Bedford.

"But let's not kid ourselves," he said at a Saturday news conference. "It will continue to break until we fix it."

He added that the transformation from copper to fiber across the ATC network is about 70% complete. 

The legacy system is known as the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI), which is managed by L3Harris Technologies (LHX). Per the company, FTI covers "4,400 facilities, manages more than 29,000 services, and supports the safe operation of 45,000 daily flights across the National Airspace System."

An upgrade from copper wires to fiber that included a router change conducted by L3Harris is to blame for Friday's nationwide ground stop, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. 

He added that AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and Lumen Technologies (LUMN) are working with the FAA on a replacement for FTI. "But in the meantime, until I can build that, I'm stuck with L3Harris, who owns this network."

Bedford maintained that until a new system is completely operational, his agency will continue to maintain the old one. He lamented there isn't enough funding to even do that properly given that a $30B request from Duffy to Congress was reduced first by the House and even more by the Senate.

He noted that ~$12.5B has been spent on modernization efforts so far.

Duffy recently called on Congress to approve $50B in funding for ATC upgrades.

data.title: Home heating oil price declines from October high but still up 59% YoY
data.description:
• The price per gallon of No. 2 home heating oil declined to $5.915 a gallon as of Nov. 9, the second weekly decline in a row, but still ~70% higher than the year-ago period.
  • Residential heating oil reached a 2026 high on Oct. 23 of $6.23, according to the US Energy Information Administration. Since the EIA began tracking home heating oil prices in October 1990, it has never reached that high. 
  • On Nov. 3, 2025, the price per gallon was $3.632. On Nov. 4, 2025, it was $3.486.
  • In October, the EIA predicted that consumers in the Northeast may not be as financially impacted as anticipated this winter as temperatures are not expected to be as cold as last year. That being said, the agency still predicts oil-heated homes could spend up to 21% more this winter on the fuel.

data.title: L3Harris upgrade to communications system preceded ground stop: Duffy
data.description:
Friday's nationwide ground stop that led to the cancellations of thousands of flights into Saturday happened after an update was made to an older communications system used by air traffic controllers and managed by L3Harris Technologies (LHX).

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said at a Saturday morning news conference that the upgrade involved switching over from copper wires to a fiber network. "What we're working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error, installator error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router."

The router in question then started flooding other routers in the nation's air traffic control system with more than one thousand connection attempts every few seconds, Duffy noted. 

"What that did is it gave us issues with communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruptions with our radar feeds."  

At a Friday news conference, Duffy blamed the ground stop on outdated equipment, adding he would like some $50B to modernize the air traffic control system.

"President Trump has asked for the money," the secretary said Friday night.  "He's asked the Congress on a bipartisan approach to say, 'Give us the resources to build a state-of-the-art air traffic control system.'" Let's not do a patchwork fix to a system that's critical for every single family. It's not red, it's not blue, it's not Democrat, it's not Republican, it's American. Give us the money to fix it."

data.title: Insider trades: Microsoft, Netflix, Boeing among notable names
data.description:

data.title: Musk defends Huang, says NVIDIA will have supply chain issues without him
data.description:
• SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk said that NVIDIA (NVDA) will suffer from supply chain issues with former CEO Jensen Huang ousted.
  •  "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," the Tesla (TSLA) CEO said in a Saturday morning X post. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
  • Musk made the comment in response to an Nov. 12 interview SemiAnalysis CEO Dylan Patel had with CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia."
  • "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through," Musk wrote in a separate Saturday morning post. "Sure, we'd put together a purchase order at some point later, but I never for a second thought it wouldn't happen."
  • On Friday, Musk said there is a petition circulating to have Huang reinstated, and he will sign it.

data.title: Former NVIDIA CEO Huang misled top execs on businesswoman relationship: report
data.description:
• Jensen Huang, who recently resigned as CEO of NVIDIA (NVDA), misled fellow top executives, including the general counsel, about his relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US intelligence alleges was recruited as a spy for China.
  • Reuters broke the story, citing internal communications it had obtained and two individuals familiar with the matter.
  • General Counsel Tim Teter and Chief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld are among those who were deceived.
  • Alice Huang is a former managing director/CEO at Megaspeed, as well as a prior controlling shareholder. The company is under scrutiny for allegedly providing chips to Chinese companies as an NVIDIA Cloud Partner without getting permission from the US government as required due to chip export controls to China.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco in focus
SpaceX still planning for Starship launch pad catch Saturday afternoon
data.description:
• An attempt to have SpaceX's (SPCX) upper stage Starship return to earth upright on a launch pad from orbit is still on schedule for around 420p ET Saturday in south Texas even though the company's Super Heavy booster on Friday diverted to an ocean splashdown instead of returning to the launch tower as well.
  • If successful, the Mechazilla launch tower's mechanical arms will "catch" Starship upright, marking the first time ever this has been done for a rocket.
  • At around 2p ET, flight controllers will make a final decision on whether to push ahead with the catch landing or divert to a splashdown off Hawaii.
  • "Starship and its heatshield are healthy as the vehicle continues to orbit Earth after a spectacular start to its mission nearly 7 hours ago," SpaceX said in an X post at 1244a ET. "Teams are continuing to monitor systems ahead of a planned return to launch site catch at Starbase ~22.5 hours after launch."

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, as investors assessed the uncertainty in the broader AI space following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs.

Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Nvidia hit with downgrades after Jensen Huang ouster

Nvidia (NVDA) saw a wave of downgrades and price-target cuts this week as analysts warned that the leadership uncertainty could weigh on the stock.

William Blair downgraded Nvidia to Market Perform, saying Huang's likely departure and heightened scrutiny of the company would be a "significant overhang on Nvidia shares in the near term." Evercore downgraded Nvidia to In Line and cut its price target to $186, from $330, citing the prospect of further valuation multiple compression.

Meanwhile, Melius Research cut the stock to Hold, saying it was difficult to assess the situation, comparing it with Hewlett-Packard's leadership crisis in 2010. KeyBanc also downgraded the company to Sector Weight from Overweight, citing increased strategic, organizational, and execution risks.

RBC lowered its PT to $230 from $330 but maintained its Outperform rating, saying a potential change at the top and congressional hearings could create an overhang. Oppenheimer cut it to Market Perform.

“As said, the uncertainty is likely to linger and turned out to be a real announcement by Nvidia, considering Jensen’s leadership is crucial to Nvidia (as well as the AI industry).” GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu wrote and lowered his rating on Nvidia to Hold from Buy, while cutting his price target to $188 from $235.

Earlier in the week, Morgan Stanley removed its top pick label on Nvidia.

Broadcom in focus after Rothschild downgrade

Rothschild & Co. downgraded Broadcom (AVGO) to Neutral, while adding there is potential upside to be had for investors.

“Guidance implies Broadcom trades at 11x FY28 EPS,” said Rothschild analyst Mike Harrison. “But this counts for little when both the quality and the durability of earnings are under scrutiny.

Harrison also lowered his price target on Broadcom to $398 from $595.

“Broadcom’s alignment with Anthropic and OpenAI means the frontier labs need to establish sustained primacy over open models and become self-financing in short order. Beyond this, the market needs reassurance that Google’s customer-owned tooling efforts will not become widespread. The upside potential to Broadcom shares from clearing these hurdles is appreciable but is unlikely to occur quickly,” he added.

AMD upgraded on potential benefit from Nvidia falloutWilliam Blair upgraded AMD (AMD) to Outperform from Market Perform, citing an opportunity to benefit from the Nvidia (NVDA) related fallout.

“We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio,” William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji said.

Naji also pointed out that the Dr. Lisa Su-led AMD is “in the early innings of a multiyear earnings growth trajectory as it continues to execute in server CPUs.”

Palo Alto upgraded ahead of Q1 results

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) was upgraded to Overweight by KeyBanc Capital Markets ahead of the cybersecurity firm reporting fiscal first-quarter results on Nov. 18.

"We are upgrading shares of PANW to Overweight as we expect security budgets to accelerate through 2027, Palo a leading beneficiary of the trend toward consolidation with strong product offerings in key areas to secure AI and defend against the accelerated AI threat environment, and Palo out-executing many of its cyber peers," analyst Eric Heath wrote and put a $380 price target on Palo Alto shares.

Roblox downgraded to Neutral by Citi

Citi downgraded Roblox (RBLX) to Neutral from Buy, citing concerns over slowing engagement and potential risks to bookings growth. The brokerage maintained its $55 price target.

Citi analyst Jason Bazinet flagged four areas of concern, including waning popularity of Steal An Egg, a lack of emerging hit experiences, potential competition from Grand Theft Auto VI, and uncertainty around booking growth.

Loop Capital upgraded Autodesk (ADSK) to Buy from Hold, citing improving growth expectations.

Baird upgraded Domino's Pizza (DPZ) to Outperform from its previous rating, citing a clearer path to improved same-store sales and franchisee profitability. The brokerage also raised its price target to $400 from $320.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: All 10 reporting firms beat EPS estimates across seven sectors; 8 grow Y/Y profits
data.description:
Earnings season continues with 10 companies reporting quarterly results across utilities, industrials, financials, energy, communication services, materials, and information technology.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, all 10 exceeded EPS expectations. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth (while 1 declined and 1 had no prior-year comparison).

Top Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, 8 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Constellation Energy (CEG): advanced just over 10% post-earnings after reporting Q3 adjusted operating earnings of $5.06 per share, beating the $3.88 consensus estimate, alongside revenue of $9.55B (+45.4% Y/Y). Management raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50–$12.80 per share, citing Calpine accretion, strong commercial performance, and higher PJM capacity prices.

Ferguson Enterprises (FERG): climbed 11.22% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.03B (+9.5% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $310M, while non-GAAP EPS of $3.43 topped forecasts by $0.14. Growth was driven by 7.0% organic expansion and 2.7% from acquisitions, prompting management to raise its calendar 2026 net sales outlook to ~7% growth and narrow its adjusted operating margin target to 9.6%–9.8%.

KKR & Co. (KKR): climbed 2.0% post-earnings after delivering Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.78, surpassing the $1.58 consensus estimate, while revenue reached $2.61B (+8.8% Y/Y). Results were bolstered by record fee-related earnings of $1.32B and strong returns in infrastructure (+4%) and alternative credit (+3%), with the firm expecting to return over $40B to clients in 2026.

NRG Energy (NRG): gained just over 10% alongside a broader utility rally after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.47B (+24.0% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $180M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.68, topping forecasts by $1.65. Management reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.90–$9.90 and projected 2027 adjusted EPS of $8.05–$10.05 ($9.05 midpoint).

Occidental Petroleum (OXY): rose 2.04% post-earnings after reporting better-than-expected Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.91 (beating by $0.44), even as revenue of $6.56B missed consensus estimates. A 32.5% Y/Y jump in average realized oil prices to $85.91/bbl helped offset a 2.5% dip in global production to 1.43M boe/day caused by maintenance and Gulf of Mexico curtailments, with Q4 output guided to 1.43M–1.47M boe/day, with output from the Permian Basin expected to ‌come in at 820K-840K boe/day.

Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO): rose 8.31% post-earnings in reaction to its FQ2 results and GTA 6 update, despite total net bookings falling 18% Y/Y to $1.60B (missing the $1.66B estimate) and EPS coming in at $1.00. Looking ahead, the company guided FY27 revenue to $8.0B–$8.2B and EPS to $0.57–$0.75, trailing consensus estimates.

TransDigm Group (TDG): rose 0.55% post-earnings as a soft profit outlook overshadowed a Q4 beat, with revenue rising 22.6% Y/Y to $2.99B (beating by ~$40M) and adjusted EPS of $12.44 topping the $12.21 consensus. While management projected FY27 revenue of $11.95B–$12.15B above estimates, its FY27 adjusted EPS forecast of $47.09–$47.94 fell short of the $48.66 consensus amid higher borrowing costs.

Vylor Inc. (VYLR): fell 0.06% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $938M (-0.6% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $19.94M, while non-GAAP EPS of -$0.42 topped expectations by $0.10. Supported by continued technology adoption, the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook for adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of ~$2.8B and EPS of $2.25–$2.35 vs. consensus of $2.38.

Applied Materials (AMAT): rose 1.4% in extended trading after reporting Q4 FY2026 revenue of $10.41B (+53% Y/Y), surpassing the $10.3B estimate, while adjusted EPS of $4.16 beat the $4.05 consensus. Fueled by strong AI-driven semiconductor demand, the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $10.6B–$11.6B ($11.1B midpoint) and adjusted EPS to $4.15–$4.55 ($4.35 midpoint), both above Street forecasts.

Cisco Systems (CSCO): perked up 2% in early post-market trading after Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 24% Y/Y to $18.5B (beating the $18.13B estimate) and adjusted EPS of $1.40 topped the $1.33 consensus. Performance was propelled by 43% Y/Y growth in networking ($11.13B), prompting Cisco to raise its FY2027 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.47–$5.52 and revenue guidance to $74.8B–$75.8B, with AI hyperscaler revenue expected to reach $9B.

Earnings next week:

As earnings season rolls on, investors are tracking key reports across communication services, consumer discretionary, consumer staples, and information technology.

Key reports to watch include The Walt Disney Company (DIS), The Home Depot (HD), Lowe's Companies (LOW), Ross Stores (ROST), The TJX Companies (TJX), Target Corporation (TGT), Tyson Foods (TSN), Walmart (WMT), NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), Intuit (INTU), Keysight Technologies (KEYS), and Everpure (P).
